subject: pathology
title: Nomenclature, characteristics and spread of tumours

steps.tx: A **neoplasm** is an abnormal new growth whose proliferation is not matched by the normal stimuli. Tumours are named by their cell of origin: a smooth muscle tumour is a leiomyoma when benign and a leiomyosarcoma when malignant. Benign tumours usually take the suffix **oma**, while malignant epithelial tumours are **carcinomas** and malignant mesenchymal tumours are **sarcomas**. Exceptions such as melanoma, seminoma, lymphoma and hepatoma are malignant despite the suffix.

steps.tx: **Differentiation** describes how closely tumour cells resemble their normal counterparts. **Anaplasia** is the loss of structural and functional differentiation and is a hallmark of malignancy. **Dysplasia** is disorderly, non-neoplastic epithelial change that can precede cancer, graded mild, moderate or severe. **Metaplasia** is the reversible replacement of one adult cell type by another, as seen in columnar to squamous change in smokers' airways.

steps.tx: **Carcinoma in situ** is full-thickness atypia of epithelium with an intact basement membrane, so no invasion is present. Invasion is shown by breaching the basement membrane or nests of cells in the dermis. Dysplasia involves only the lower layers of the epidermis, whereas carcinoma in situ extends to the surface. Matrix metalloproteinases help tumour cells invade by remodelling the basement membrane and interstitial matrix, while loss of **E-cadherin** weakens cell to cell adhesion.

steps.tx: Spread occurs by three routes. **Lymphatic spread** is the commonest route for carcinomas and follows natural drainage; the **sentinel lymph node** is the first node receiving flow from the tumour, and skip metastasis can occur. **Haematogenous spread** is typical of sarcomas and veins are invaded more often than arteries. Portal drainage sends tumour to the liver and caval blood to the lung. **Seeding** into body cavities, especially peritoneal, is characteristic of ovarian carcinoma.

steps.tx: Benign developmental lesions are classed by tissue location. A **hamartoma** is normal tissue in a normal site, such as a skin birthmark. A **choristoma** is normal tissue in an abnormal site, such as pancreatic tissue in the duodenum, so ectopic rest of normal tissue is a choristoma. A **teratoma** contains tissue from all three germ layers and arises from totipotent cells, mainly in gonads. Mature teratomas are benign and immature teratomas are malignant.
